title: Bohn Hall Community Meeting
description:
Join us for the Bohn Hall Community Meeting! This is your opportunity to connect with your Professional Staff, student staff, and fellow residents as we kick off the semester together. At this meeting, we’ll cover important information about living in Bohn Hall, including community expectations, resources, and ways to get involved. 
 Residents will also have the chance to ask questions, share feedback, and meet others in the building. Attendance is encouraged to stay up-to-date and make the most out of your living experience on campus.

title: Play & Prep: Snacks & Games with CAST x University Libraries
description:

You can play a game with our friendly fall academic support crew—Librarians, Peer Tutors & Peer Academic Coaches, —and enjoy some tasty snacks. Feel free to kick back with friends in our usual tutoring spaces or start a board game. Visitors can also create their own personal pin a for the semester. Our staff are eager to join in the fun or share their favorite tips for a successful semester. 
 Got a quick question or want to set up an appointment to kick off the semester strong? We’re here to help! Plus, everyone attending will get first dibs on booking for our Fall 2026 tutoring & peer coaching sessions. Hope to see you there!

title: Montclair Mixtape: Build-a-Zine with WMSC
description:
What if you could bottle up the very beginning of your Montclair story? 
 Montclair Mixtape  is a collaborative Welcome Week zine where every student gets to create a page that captures  who they are right now —their favorite songs, big goals, random interests, and everything they hope to experience during their first year at Montclair. 
 Then, make it yours! Decorate your page with  stickers, doodles, magazine cutouts, colors, lyrics, photos, or anything else that feels like you.  While creating, students can chat, swap recommendations, discover shared interests, and get to know the people around them. 
 Throughout Welcome Week, pages will be collected and brought together into one giant collaborative  “Montclair Mixtape” zine —a snapshot of the students, dreams, personalities, and playlists that make up YOUR first week on campus. 
 With student permission, the finished zine can be shared digitally through  Canva , creating a time capsule students can revisit long after Welcome Week is over. 
 Because your first week isn't just the beginning of college— it's the first page of your Montclair story.  🎧📖

title: Finding your Center Workshop
description:
Finding Your Civic Voice.  Your Voice Has Power. Come learn wow to use it. 
 Kick off the semester by discovering the power of your voice! As part of Weeks of Welcome, Civic and Voter Engagement invites you to Finding Your Civic Voice, an interactive workshop designed to help you connect your passions with meaningful civic action. 
 Through engaging activities and guided discussion, you'll explore what civic voice means, reflect on the issues that matter most to you, and identify how your unique experiences and perspectives can make a difference. Whether you're passionate about education, the environment, mental health, social justice, or another cause, this workshop will help you transform your ideas into action. 
 Together, we'll explore how everyday actions—such as voting, volunteering, advocating, or engaging in respectful dialogue—can strengthen your community and create lasting impact. You'll also learn how to communicate your perspective in a clear and meaningful way while developing an achievable next step to stay involved throughout your time at Montclair State. 
 Participants will: 
 
 Explore what civic voice is and why it matters 
 Identify an issue they're passionate about 
 Develop a concise message that reflects their values and experiences 
 Leave with a practical action plan to begin making a difference 
 
 Whether you're new to civic engagement or already involved, this workshop is a great opportunity to meet fellow students, share ideas, and start the year with purpose. Join us during Weeks of Welcome and discover how your voice can help shape both our campus and our communities.

description:

description:
The 9/11 National Day of Service and Remembrance is long standing tradition at Montclair State University that honors the lives lost and heroic acts of September 11, 2001. Our volunteers commemorate the day through meaningful service projects that foster unity, civic responsibility, leadership, and often inspire long-term community engagement. 
 Come join us for a day of giving back! 
 Volunteers will have the opportunity to choose from 20+ service sites, both on and off campus, and engage in community service projects such as: 
 
 🍎 Meal distribution and food pantry support 
 🌳 Park and neighborhood cleanups 
 🎨 Community revitalization 
 ✨ Activities for youth, seniors, and adults with disabilities 
 🧼 Assembling hygiene and snack kits 
  And much more! 
 
 Here’s what you can expect: 
 
 ⏰ Registration  at 8:00 - 8:30 AM. Event starts at  8:30 AM 
 🚌  Transportation provided  to and from off-campus sites 
 🥯  Free breakfast and lunch  to fuel your day 
 ⏳  Service hours  validation (for students/groups that need it) 
 👕 Exclusive 9/11 Day of Service T-Shirt 
 🧑‍🎓 Bloomfield College  students will have a shuttle service provided 
 🎊 Icebreaker activities and giveaways! 
 
   
 IMPORTANT NOTE:  You can only sign up for  one  service site due to each project running simultaneously. We will email you after registration if other information is needed for your site. 
 Sign up link: https://www.eventzilla.net/e/911-national-day-of-service-and-remembrance-2026-2138674558

title: 9/11 day of Service: Campus Blitz
description:
Honor the spirit of service on Montclair State University's Annual 9/11 Day of Service by helping ensure every eligible Red Hawk has the opportunity to make their voice heard. 
 Join the Office of Civic and Voter Engagement for Race to the Ballot: Campus Takeover, a campus-wide service initiative that empowers students to become civic ambassadors. During this hands-on volunteer experience, you'll learn how to confidently engage your peers in nonpartisan conversations about voting, assist them with the voter registration process, and encourage them to make a pledge to show up on Election Day. 
 No previous experience or political knowledge is required—just a willingness to serve your campus community and help others participate in our democracy. Our team will provide all the training, resources, and support you need to feel comfortable talking with fellow students and answering common questions about voter registration and upcoming elections. 
 As New Jersey's voter registration deadline approaches, volunteers will work alongside Civic and Voter Engagement staff to reach students across campus through pop-up voter registration stations and outreach efforts. Together, we'll help ensure every student has access to accurate, trusted, and nonpartisan election information. 
 As a volunteer, you will learn how to: 
 
 Assist students with registering to vote or updating their voter registration 
 Encourage fellow students to pledge to vote on Election Day 
 Answer common questions about voter registration and voting options 
 Connect students with trusted, nonpartisan election resources 
 Engage in respectful, nonpartisan conversations about civic participation 
 Help create a campus culture that values democratic engagement 
 
 By participating, you'll gain valuable leadership, communication, and outreach skills while making a meaningful impact on campus. Every conversation has the potential to inspire someone to participate in our democracy, and every new voter strengthens our community. 
 Whether you're passionate about civic engagement or simply looking for a meaningful way to give back on the 9/11 Day of Service, this is an opportunity to serve your fellow students while helping build a more informed, engaged, and connected campus. 
 No experience is necessary—just bring your enthusiasm, a willingness to make a difference, and a commitment to serving others. Together, we'll help every Red Hawk get election ready, one conversation at a time.

title: (Montclair Campus) National Voter Registration Day: Race to the Ballot
description:
Join thousands of colleges, universities, nonprofits, businesses, and community organizations across the country as we celebrate National Voter Registration Day—the nation's largest single-day voter registration effort. This annual, nonpartisan initiative brings Americans together with one shared goal: helping eligible voters get registered, informed, and prepared to participate in our democracy. 
 Join us on September 17 from 12:00–4:00 PM in the Student Center Ballrooms and on the Quad as Montclair State University celebrates this national movement with an afternoon of civic engagement, entertainment, and community. 
 This year's event is proudly presented in collaboration with the Office of Commuter Life as part of Commuter Life Appreciation Week (CLAW). Together, we're celebrating the important role commuter students play in our campus community while encouraging every Red Hawk to become an informed and engaged participant in our democracy. 
 Whether you're registering to vote for the first time, updating your voter registration, or learning more about the upcoming election, Race to the Ballot is your one-stop destination to get election ready. 
 The event will kick off with welcoming remarks from Montclair State University President Dr. Jonathan Koppell, who will officially open the celebration by speaking about the importance of civic participation and the power of student voices. Throughout the afternoon, you'll also hear from special guest speakers who will share their perspectives on the importance of voting, civic leadership, and making a difference in our communities. 
 Enjoy a fun-filled afternoon featuring: 
 
 A giant patriotic inflatable obstacle course 
 Yard games and interactive activities 
 Free food served throughout the event 
 Music, giveaways, and civic swag 
 Voter registration assistance and nonpartisan election resources 
 Interactive activities hosted by campus and community partners 
 
 Be sure to stay for the entire event! Students who remain through the closing program will be entered into a raffle for a chance to win an exciting grand prize. 
 Together, we're joining a nationwide effort that has helped millions of Americans prepare to vote. Race to the Ballot is more than a voter registration event—it's a celebration of civic participation, community, and the belief that every voice has the power to shape the future. 
 The race starts here. The finish line is the ballot box. Register, get informed, and join the movement!

title: Kayaking on the Delaware River
description:
Enjoy a relaxing day paddling down the Delaware River and learn some basic kayaking skills. Leaving from Montclair State University, NJ, this full-day trip will provide you with a chance to enjoy the warm, clear waters of the longest undammed river east of the Mississippi. We provide the boats, life jackets and paddles, but be prepared to get wet. 
   How do I Sign-up? 
 
 Register  here  or in the Student Rec Center main office, or over the phone (973-655-3340). 
 Cost for Students $10;  $20  Faculty/Staff 
 
 Where and When? 
 
 September 19th, 2026 
 9:00 am – 6:00 pm    
 Begins at Student Recreation Center 
 
 What to bring:  Water, lunch, bathing suit, towel, sunblock and a change of clothes. 
   
 Potential Hazards:  under/above water obstructions, rapidly moving water, poisonous plants/allergies, insect bites, unpredictable weather changes, sunburn/heat exhaustion, dehydration

title: Find the Sources You Need
description:
Learn where and how to search for books, articles, and more. We’ll break down the differences between primary and secondary sources. We'll discuss "credible sources," both those from scholarly (peer-reviewed) journals and those from other sources. We'll also discuss, among other things, the differences between our two largest family of databases -- ProQuest and EBSCO. We want you to advance your searching skills so that you learn to have fun searching (a.k.a. researching). A perfect workshop if you’re new to college-level research or you just want to sharpen your skills before your next assignment. 
 Register Here:  https://montclair.libcal.com/event/17454786

title: AEW: MAJOR KICKOFF 2026
location: The Student Center Ballrooms ABC + Patio / The Quad + Flagpoles
description:
Major Kickoff a high-energy, campus-wide event that transforms a traditional majors fair into an interactive and dynamic experience that sets the tone for major exploration.  Major Kickoff  serves as a central hub where exploratory ("undeclared") students can dive into the wide array of majors offered at Montclair in a fun and engaging way. Students will engage with peers, faculty, and staff; discover pathways to get involved in various programs; and gain the guidance they need to make confident, informed decisions about their major. With the opportunity to declare a major on the spot,  Major Kickoff  empowers students to take charge of their academic journey. 
 With over 50 departments, programs, clubs, and more on site, you never know what you might discover or who you might meet.  Enjoy free food, games, music, and giveaways, win prizes and T-shirts , and maybe even discover your major. 
 Major Kickoff is part of Academic Exploration Week, a longstanding immersive experience presented by The Discovery Program. To contact the Discovery Program, email us at  discoveryprogram@montclair.edu , or visit us at  montclair.edu/discovery-program .

description: The Dominoes Tournament is a Hispanic Heritage Month event hosted by Lambda Theta Phi where students will compete in teams in a dominoes tournament. title: Pride and Progress: Celebrating LGBTQ+ and Disability Journeys
description:
Join Advocacy and Outreach for our 3rd Annual LGBTQ+ and Disability History and Awareness Month Flag Raising and Reception — a joyful celebration of identity, resilience, and community! 
 Pride and Progress brings together students, faculty, and staff to honor the rich histories and vibrant futures of LGBTQ+ and disability communities. Enjoy an inspiring flag-raising ceremony featuring an energetic MC, powerful speakers, and a special live performance you won’t want to miss. 
 After the ceremony, the celebration continues with: - Music & vibes - Delicious food - A hands-on craft activity - A photo activation station - Free LGBTQ+ and Disability Pride flags - Interactive tabling from campus partners 
 This event is about visibility, solidarity, and celebration — open to everyone, including allies! Come as you are, bring your friends, and help us raise our voices (and our flags!) in honor of progress, pride, and community power.

title: Fall Symposium: Reclaiming the Narrative
description:
In celebration of Archives Month, University Libraries will highlight how primary source materials can bring marginalized stories to the center of education, advocacy, and community engagement. Dr. Melissa Benbow Flowers, Scholar‑in‑Residence at Sprague Library (2025–2026), in collaboration with Bloomfield College, will host a symposium exploring how working‑class histories and undertold stories in New Jersey are researched, interpreted, and shared with the public. The program will bring together scholars, students, museum professionals, and public historians whose work focuses on labor, domestic work, immigration, race, and community change—particularly as these histories are communicated through museums, historic sites, archives, and public‑facing scholarship. Registration is free and open to students, faculty, staff, and members of the public—but limited!  Registration closes September 18 . 
 Register Now

title: Power of Latinas: Strengthening Our Legacy
description:
LUPE Fund, Inc's  "Power of Latinas: Strengthening Our Legacy," conference and networking reception will be held at Montclair State University's Hall  Conference Center  on October 1st, 2026. LUPE Fund, Inc., New Jersey's oldest Latina-run organization, proudly celebrated its 20th anniversary in 2023.  
 The Conference Center is located at Montclair State University Campus, at University Hall on the 7th Floor.  
 Join us for an inspiring and empowering event featuring panels in health & wellness, business, politics, and education. Each panelist is a powerful and influential Latina dedicated to making a difference. Followed by a networking session, don’t miss your chance to connect with these dynamic women and gain insights that could transform your personal and professional life! Refreshments will be available.  
 Event Schedule 
 2:00 pm                             Registration Opens   
 3:00 pm                             Welcome and Keynote Speaker           
 4:00 pm                             Educate/Engage/Empower Panels 
 5:15 pm                             Eleccion Latina Panel 
 6:30 pm                             Presentation of Awards and Scholarships 
 7:30 pm                             Networking Reception  
 We welcome all students to participate! Whether you're able to join us for the full event or just a portion, this conference will offer valuable opportunities to engage.

title: Espresso Your Vote Grab a Coffee. Get Election Ready. (Montclair Campus)
description:
Start your day with coffee and conversation! Join the Office of Student Belonging and Civic and Voter Engagement for Espresso Your Vote, a welcoming pop-up event designed to help you prepare for the upcoming election. 
 Whether you need to register to vote, update your voter registration, check your registration status, or simply have questions about the voting process, our team is here to help. We'll provide trusted, nonpartisan information to ensure you have everything you need to vote with confidence. 
 Enjoy a complimentary cup of coffee while connecting with fellow students, learning about important election dates and deadlines, and discovering the many ways you can make your voice heard. 
 Stop by to: 
 
 Register to vote or update your voter registration 
 Verify your voter registration status 
 Learn about your voting options 
 Ask questions about the upcoming election 
 Grab a cup of coffee and connect with campus resources 
 
 Sometimes the best conversations happen over coffee. Take a break, enjoy a fresh cup, and leave feeling informed, prepared, and ready to participate in our democracy.

title: Broadway Trip: The Lost Boys
description:
The show is at 7 pm on October 7th, and is about 2 hours and 30 minutes long with one 15-minute intermission.  Transportation will be provided and the bus will pick up from the Red Hawk Deck at 5 pm. Attendees are encouraged to arrive at the Red Hawk Deck at 4:45 pm. The bus will leave promptly at the conclusion of the show and aims to be back to campus by 10:15 pm depending on traffic. Please direct all questions to activities@montclair.edu 
   
 When Michael moves to California with his younger brother Sam and their mother Lucy, he’s desperate to leave his old life behind and start fresh. A wild night out on the boardwalk finds him in the shadows of Santa Carla and brings him face-to-face with David, the magnetic leader of a local rock band. David and his bandmates offer Michael freedom, adventure, and the connection he’s been longing to find. But when the band’s dark secret finally comes out, Michael must decide how far he’s willing to go to belong. 
   
 Tickets will be available for purchase starting on TBD.

title: Whitewater Rafting Trip
description:
Coordinating with the release of the dam in the Lehigh River, this whitewater rafting trip is sure to be a blast. Perfect for all skill levels. This is a great way to GET YOUR FEET WET!  
   
 How do I Sign-up? 
 
 Register online through Fusion, in the Student Recreation Center's main office, or over the phone (973-655-3340). 
 Cost for Students  $20  
 
   
 Where and when? 
 
 Saturday, October 10, 2026 
 7:00am – 7:00pm 
 Begins at Student Recreation Center 
 
   
 What to bring:  Lunch, water, snacks, towel, a change of clothes and sandals with a heel strap, old sneakers, or water shoes. Flip-flops or slides are not allowed. For warmer days, wear a swim suit or quick-drying shorts/shirt; for cooler days, bring extra layers, but no cotton. Wetsuits are included for those that want them. Half/full wetsuits can be rented from the organization. Half is $6, full is $12, jacket is $4.  
   
 Potential Hazards:  Unpredictable weather changes, sunburn/heat exhaustion, limited vision, dehydration, allergic reactions/poisonous plants, insect bites and injury by running, including sprains, lacerations, abrasions and fractures.

title: All In: The Fight for Democracy Film Screening & Civic Engagement Experience
description:
Democracy doesn't protect itself—it depends on informed, engaged citizens. 
 Join Civic and Voter Engagement, in collaboration with the African American Caucus, for a powerful screening of  All In: The Fight for Democracy , the critically acclaimed documentary that examines the history and present-day reality of voter suppression in the United States. Featuring voting rights advocate Stacey Abrams, the film explores the historical barriers, systemic inequities, and ongoing challenges that continue to shape access to the ballot box and influence civic participation. 
 More than a documentary, this screening is an opportunity to deepen your understanding of the democratic process, reflect on the importance of protecting voting rights, and engage in meaningful dialogue about one of the most fundamental rights in our democracy. 
 Following the screening, participants are invited to stay for a facilitated discussion exploring the themes of the film, the significance of voting rights in today's political landscape, and the role each of us can play in strengthening our democracy through civic engagement. Whether you're new to these conversations or actively engaged in public life, this discussion offers a welcoming space to learn from one another, share perspectives, and consider how informed civic participation can create positive change. 
 Join us for: 
 
 A screening of the award-winning documentary  All In: The Fight for Democracy 
 A facilitated discussion on the film's relevance to today's political climate 
 Meaningful conversation with fellow students, faculty, and staff 
 Free food and refreshments 
 Civic-themed giveaways 
 Resources to help you stay informed and engaged 
 
 This event is open to all students, faculty, and staff. Come for the film, stay for the conversation, and leave with a deeper understanding of the importance of civic participation and the power of every voice. 
 Good film. Great conversation. Free food. Giveaways. One important conversation about the future of our democracy.

title: New Jersey's 44th Annual Law School Day
description:
Are you thinking about applying to law school? Join us for our 44th Annual NJ Law School Day at Montclair State University! All NJ college students and alumni who are interested in applying to law school are welcome to attend! 
 At NJ Law School Day, you can speak with law school representatives from NJ, NY, and across the U.S. about what their programs have to offer and how you can prepare to be a strong law school candidate.  Whether you are new to the idea of applying to law school or preparing to apply this fall, this event is a great opportunity to learn and connect. 
 
   
 What to Expect from Law School Day : 
 1pm - 2pm - Law School Panel Discussion 
 - For this session, you will hear from a panel of law school representatives about what they look for when reviewing law school applications and how to become a strong law school candidate. 
   
 2 - 4pm - The Law School Fair 
 - This is your chance to meet face-to- face with law school representatives from NJ, NY, PA, MA and across the U.S., and ask questions about applying to law school! 
 - The list of law schools attending is growing! Current law schools attending include:  American, Fordham, Villanova, Ohio State, Seton Hall, Rutgers, Drexel, Penn State, Pace, Syracuse, Cardozo, Utah, Maryland, West Virginia, Richmond, Pittsburgh , and many, many more.   
 - You can see the full list of law schools attending once you RSVP on Handshake on or after September 1, 2026 
   
 3:30 - 4:30 PM - Speed Mentoring: Pathways to Public Service 
 -  After learning what it takes to get into law school, stick around to connect directly with professionals who are doing the work.   
 - Through fast-paced, small-group rotating conversations, you’ll discover real-world career paths, and get honest insights into public interest and public service work. Come listen, ask questions, grab a snack, and make connections that can kickstart your legal, public interest, or public service career. 
   
 How to Be Prepared for Law School Day : 
 
 Be ready to share information about you, your interests, and your goals! 
 Write down the questions you have about law schools and the process of applying to law school 
 Bring something to take notes 
 Dress to impress!  Business attire is recommended 
 Registration for Law School Day will open on September 1, 2026 on Handshake 
 Questions? Need law school advice? Email Chrysten Colacicco, Pre-Law Program Coordinator at MSU, at colaciccoc@montclair.edu

title: Speed Mentoring: Pathways to Public Service
description:
Join us for the grand finale of NJ  Law  School  Day ! 
 
 
 
 After learning what it takes to get into  law  school, stick around to connect directly with professionals who are doing the work. 
 This interactive session breaks away from traditional panels to give you direct access to public service professionals, legal practitioners, community advocates, legislative staff, policy experts, and elected officials. 
 Through fast-paced, small-group rotating conversations, you’ll discover real-world career paths, and get honest insights into public interest work. Come listen, ask questions, grab a snack, and make connections that can kickstart your legal or public service career. 
 
 
 
 
 Questions?  Contact Donna Robertson at  chsscareer@montclair.edu .

title: Making It in the Arts: CART Alumni Career Panel
organization: The Office for Experiential Education and Career Connections
description:
Join alumni from the College of the Arts as they share their career journeys, discuss how they transitioned from college to the professional world, and offer advice for students interested in creative careers. 
 Panelists will discuss: 
 
 Building a career in the arts and creative industries 
 Navigating internships, auditions, and professional opportunities 
 Developing industry connections and professional networks 
 Skills that helped them succeed after graduation 
 Challenges, opportunities, and lessons learned along the way 
 
 Featured career areas include: 
 
 Performing Arts and Theater Production 
 Fashion and Apparel 
 Dance and Performance 
 Arts Administration 
 Human Resources in Creative Industries 
 
 Students will have the opportunity to ask questions, learn about different career paths, and gain firsthand insights from CART alumni who have successfully launched their careers.

title: Self Care in a Chaotic world is Radical
description: This is a self care event highlighting the importance to be holistically introspective amidst chaos and how to balance a healthy schedule for our future whilst watering our present. title: Paulinskill Rail Trail - Biking Trip
description:
Come join us on a bike through the Paulinskill rail trail, which is flat and an easy trail for anyone. This trail used to be a railroad and was made into a bike path. While biking, you will be in the nice fall weather and enjoying the outdoors. (Biking experience required) 
 How do I Sign-up? 
 
 
 Please register in the Student Rec Center main office, or over the phone (973-655-3340). 
 
 
 Cost for Students  $10 
 
 
 Where and When? 
 
 
 November 7th, 2026 
 
 
 9-5 
 
 
 Begins Student Recreation Center 
 
 
 What to bring:  Water, Lunch, Long Pants, Sneakers, and Sunscreen. 
 Potential Hazards:  unpredictable weather changes, sunburn/heat exhaustion, dehydration, allergic reactions/poisonous plants, insect bites, injury by running including sprains, lacerations, abrasions and fractures.

title: Major & Career Exploration Talks: What We Wish We Knew Before Declaring!
description:
Not sure what major to choose or where your career path is headed? You’re not alone! Join us for  Major & Career Exploration Talks: What We Wish We Knew Before Declaring! , a dynamic panel event where upperclassmen students share their real, unfiltered experiences about choosing their majors and navigating their career journeys. Hear firsthand what they wish they knew before declaring, the challenges they faced, and how they found their passions. Whether you're feeling undecided, overwhelmed, or just curious about different paths, this event will give you insights, inspiration, and practical advice to help you make informed decisions. Don’t miss this opportunity to gain valuable perspectives and take the next step in your academic and career journey! * Food and refreshments will be served! 
 This workshop is presented by  The Discovery Program . To contact the Discovery Program, email us at  discoveryprogram@montclair.edu , or visit us at  montclair.edu/discovery-program .

title: Transgender Awareness Week Flag Raising & Gathering
description:
Join Advocacy & Outreach in the Office of Student Belonging at our Trans Awareness Week flag raising to commemorate the start of Trans Awareness Week. 
 We will receive words from some of our students 
 The flag raising is at the Student Center Flag poles from 2:00pm - 2:30pm 
 The gathering after is at the Advocacy & Outreach Office, Suite 113 of the Student Center from 2:30pm - 3:30pm 
 All are welcome!

title: Find the Sources You Need
description:
Learn where and how to search for books, articles, and more.  We’ll break down the differences between primary and secondary sources.  We'll discuss "credible sources," both those from scholarly (peer-reviewed) journals and those from other sources.  We'll also discuss, among other things, the differences between our two largest family of databases -- ProQuest and EBSCO. We want you to advance your searching skills so that you learn to have fun searching (a.k.a. researching). A perfect workshop if you’re new to college-level research or you just want to sharpen your skills before your next assignment. 
 Register Here:  https://montclair.libcal.com/event/17454788

title: Turtle Back Zoo
description:
Join your friends for a day at the Zoo! See animals from all over the world as you enjoy lunch at your choice of cafes around the park. Bring cash for lunch, a water bottle to stay hydrated, and comfortable walking shoes. 
   
 How do I sign-up? 
 
 Register  here  or in the Student Rec Center main office, or over the phone (973-655-3340). 
 Cost for Students  $20 
 
   
 Where and when? 
 
 November 21 2026  
 10am-4pm 
 Begins at Student Recreation Center 
 
   
 What to bring:  Water, lunch, long pants, sneakers, and sunscreen.   Participants MUST wear sneakers in order to go on the zipline and obstacle course. 
   
 Note:  Tree Top Adventures restricts obstacle course and zipline participants to a strict weight limit of 250 lbs. Students may opt to participate in only the Zoo portion of the trip should they like. 
   
 Potential Hazards:  Unpredictable weather changes, sunburn/heat exhaustion, dehydration, allergic reactions/poisonous plants, insect bites and injury by running, including sprains, lacerations, abrasions and fractures.

 Troilus and Cressida  (play) is a dark, satirical take on love and war during the Trojan War. Troilus and Cressida’s romance is tested when she is traded to the Greek camp, while warriors and leaders on both sides reveal ambition, ego, and moral decay. The play questions heroism, loyalty, and what’s left of love in a world defined by conflict.

title: Women's History Month Flag Raising & Reception
description:
Attention Montclair + Bloomfield Communities! 
   
 Get ready to raise the flag at the A&O annual Women's History Month flag raising and reception! 
 Join us Monday, March 1, 2027 to come together and honor the incredible achievements and ongoing impact of the women who make our campus community and world at large shine bright. 
 We'll begin with a special  flag raising ceremony at 12:30 PM in the Student Center Flag Pole  to collectively lift up the trailblazing women who have paved the way for us all. 
   
 Then, head over to the  Student Center Ballroom A&B  from 1:00 - 2:00 PM for a reception  you won't want to miss. We'll be mixing, mingling, eating, partying, crafting, and highlighting the talent, passion, and brilliance of the inspiring women in our midst. 
 This is your chance to celebrate, connect, and show some serious school spirit. Bring your energy, bring your pride, and get ready for an unforgettable afternoon! 
   
 Tell a friend to tell a friend. We can't wait to see you there!

title: "Phaedra" by Elizabeth Egloff
description:
Written by  Elizabeth Egloff  | Directed by  Debbie Saivetz 
 Set in a timeless, surreal Mediterranean landscape, "Phaedra" by Elizabeth Egloff is a reimagining of the classical myth that shifts the focus from grand public tragedy to a deeply personal experience of solitude, longing, and memory. The story is told by a mysterious Narrator who is haunted by the memory of Phaedra, a Queen paralyzed by a forbidden passion for her stepson, Hippolytus. As Phaedra languishes on her daybed, attended by her Nurse and observed by a chatty, opinionated Chorus, the world around her takes on a dreamlike quality where a sewing machine clatters with the rhythm of a heart and the landscape is an itemization of blue, leaving every character adrift in a sea of unrequited memory. When Phaedra finally breaks her silence to confront Hippolytus, her confession leads not to connection but to a psychic "emptying" of herself. The play concludes with the Narrator left in his own solitude, haunted by the echoes of those who have passed away.

title: Denim Day: Mind the Gaps, Move Forward
description:
April is Sexual Assault Awareness Month, and together, we can break the silence.  The Montclair State University Police Department and the Office of Advocacy & Outreach are committed to fostering a campus where survivors feel heard, supported, and empowered.  It starts with believing. It starts with you.  By offering a safe and affirming response to those who disclose gender-based and sexual violence, we can create lasting change. Let’s stand together to end the cycle of silence—because  every voice matters, and every action counts. 
 Denim Day is recognized internationally as a day of action and awareness, encouraging people to wear denim to challenge victim-blaming and educate others about sexual violence.  This year, Denim Day falls on Wednesday, April 28, 2027. 
 The University Police and  Office of Advocacy & Outreach and the Office of Advocacy and Community Resilience , in partnership with over 30 campus and local community organizations, invites you to join us  from 9 a.m. to 12 p.m. at the Amphitheater  for a powerful awareness event honoring survivors and increasing awareness of available resources. 
 Despite the  gaps  that still exist in the criminal justice system, in resources, and in prevention education,  we will move forward together  as a community. As part of this commitment, we will walk  one mile around campus in solidarity with survivors.
